prompt.context: Mediplus is a US-based health plan company that operates primarily in the US. Mediplus recently announced that it is merging with another big player in the market, Globus. Globus is also a health plan company that operates in the US, South America, and Europe. The merged entity will become the third largest health plan company in the US and will try to exploit economies of scale, increased reach, and diversified product portfolio as sources of competitive advantages in the health plan industry. As our firm has already delivered some stellar work for both firms in the past few years, we have been engaged to help the new entity create a comprehensive integration plan. The partner on the project has a meeting with the head of the client's integration team tomorrow and has asked for your help to brainstorm a possible high-level plan that he can present to the client tomorrow.
prompt.question: The partner wants you to: (1) Look at integrating the two cultures; (2) Think about the differences in business operation models of the two companies; (3) Think about the broad timelines. Consider the interviewer as that partner and take them through your thinking on creating this high-level integration plan.

clarifying_info.q: Are both players selling similar or the same products? What are the differences in customer base or go-to-market approach?
clarifying_info.a: Although both players sell health insurance, Mediplus is strong in Medicare plans (government-funded insurance programs for senior citizens and a few corporate clients), whereas Globus is a strong Preferred Provider Organization (PPO) plan company (selling insurance to all people but restricting them to a network of preferred providers — doctors, hospitals, pharmacies, etc.). The merger will give access to newer customers and provide opportunities for cross-selling.

clarifying_info.q: Has the client given us specific timelines?
clarifying_info.a: The client is looking at a 2-year integration plan.

clarifying_info.q: Was there anything that came out as a priority concern in due diligence?
clarifying_info.a: The differences between the technologies used was an area of concern. While Globus has all new internal systems, Mediplus is still struggling with legacy systems that need an upgrade.

clarifying_info.q: Is there any difference in size or in geographic locations of the two companies?
clarifying_info.a: Globus is currently 1.5 times as big as Mediplus and has a strong structured culture compared to Mediplus, which has a culture like a startup. The two companies have decided to have two product headquarters and are not looking at shutting or moving any office for the next 2 years.

framework: Option A — Lifecycle framework: Present the solution as a series of next steps with appropriate level of detail to be achieved over a defined period of time (can look like a Gantt chart)

Option B — Work Streams framework: Go deeper into all work streams (Talent Acquisition, Talent Management, Organization Design, Culture, Rewards, HR Operations, Talent Development, Internal Communications)

Option C — People–Process–Technology framework: Divide activities by area of impact — People (shared vision, org structure, talent assessment, benefits alignment), Process (performance management, process design, hand-offs, synergies), Technology (assess and align systems such as SAP vs. Oracle, outsourcing design and implementation)

questions.prompt: How would you approach integrating the two cultures given Globus's structured corporate culture versus Mediplus's startup-like culture?
questions.guidance: Strong answer identifies the cultural gap (structured vs. startup), proposes creating a shared vision and aligning leadership early, uses change management and communications throughout the lifecycle, and acknowledges the complexity of two product headquarters coexisting for 2 years.

questions.prompt: What are the key differences in business operating models between the two companies and how does that affect integration?
questions.guidance: Strong answer notes: (1) Product difference — Medicare (senior/government) vs. PPO (broad network); (2) Cross-sell opportunity — Medicare clients can be offered PPO and vice versa; (3) Geography — Globus operates in US, South America, Europe vs. Mediplus US-only; (4) Size — Globus is 1.5x larger; (5) Technology gap — Globus on modern systems, Mediplus on legacy; these differences drive integration complexity and sequencing.

questions.prompt: What broad timelines would you propose for the 2-year integration plan?
questions.guidance: Strong answer sequences activities logically, e.g.: Year 1 — establish shared vision and leadership alignment, assess talent, define new org structure, begin technology assessment and road-mapping, launch communications; Year 2 — execute technology migration/upgrade, align benefits and HR policies, capture operational synergies, finalize org design. Candidate may frame this as a Gantt-style phased plan.

brainstorming.prompt: What are all the work streams that need to be addressed in this integration?

categories.name: People
ideas: Create a shared vision for the merged entity
Align leadership and establish decision rights
Align compensation, benefits, and HR policies
Internal communications and change management throughout lifecycle

categories.name: Process
ideas: Align performance management systems (rating scales, timelines)
Define go-to-market approach for cross-selling Medicare and PPO products

categories.name: Technology
ideas: Assess current systems (Globus new systems vs. Mediplus legacy)
Develop roadmap to upgrade or replace Mediplus legacy systems
Evaluate outsourcing options for non-core technology functions
Align technology platforms to support integrated operations

categories.name: Culture
ideas: Define target culture for the merged entity
Use change leaders to drive customized communications

recommendation: Adopt a People–Process–Technology framework organized into a 2-year phased Gantt-style roadmap
Year 1 priority: create shared vision, align leadership, conduct talent assessment, and begin technology gap analysis given the legacy-system risk flagged in due diligence
Year 2 priority: execute technology migration, finalize org design, align HR policies, and activate cross-sell strategy leveraging the complementary Medicare and PPO portfolios
risks: Technology integration risk is high — Mediplus legacy systems could delay the broader integration and create operational disruptions
Cultural clash between Globus's structured culture and Mediplus's startup culture may cause talent attrition, especially at Mediplus
Two product headquarters with no office consolidation for 2 years may slow decision-making and create confusion over accountability
Regulatory risk — health plan mergers are subject to government scrutiny; integration timeline may be affected by regulatory approval conditions
next_steps: Confirm the integration governance structure and appoint an Integration Management Office (IMO)
Commission a technology assessment to size the legacy system upgrade cost and timeline
Launch a culture diagnostic survey at both organizations
Develop a detailed communications plan for employees, customers, and regulators
